sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

Case M23: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 270x270x729 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case M23 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(270, 270, 729) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: myxoid soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 364/729 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm seeing a large lesion in the thigh, so I want to check the coronal view to assess its full extent.

content.text: sheet axial 250–500/729 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 2/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: The tumor appears to span roughly slices 310-460 in the medial thigh, within the adductor compartment, while the lower slices around 250-295 show a feathery signal pattern that looks more like peritumoral edema than actual tumor. I should check the coronal view around slice 135 for markers, but first I'll place a reference point on axial slice 364.

content.text: axial 364/729 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: The image seems mirrored with patient right on the left, femur positioned center-right. The bright oval is the tumor, while that posterior tail region looks intermediate, possibly edema or muscle. I'll place points at several locations within the tumor itself.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 1558.4 mL | components 30 (largest 99.9%; 29 others total 0.1 mL) | extent axial 214–529, coronal 74–236, sagittal 78–215 | change +1558.4 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 4/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (4 mark(s)) | image: axial 370, coronal 160, sagittal 150 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
I'm checking whether the reported volume of 1558 mL is plausible given the mask's apparent dimensions across slices—roughly estimating it as an ellipsoid spanning about 140x100x150 mm, which lines up reasonably well, though the axial extent of 214-529 might include small disconnected fragments.

I should focus on keeping just the largest connected component rather than these spike-like extensions, and I want to pick a coordinate inside it to use as a marker—2521 seems like a candidate. The superior spike appears connected to the main mass, so I should look at sagittal slice 150 to understand what's happening there.

content.text: sagittal 150/270 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm cross-referencing the sagittal scaling with the axial slices to figure out whether the superior spike is tumor extending along the adductors or obturator region, and I'm reconsidering that bright box in slice 477 — it's likely the bladder on the patient's right side rather than tumor.

Let me check the coronal series next to better understand the superior extent.

content.text: sheet coronal 90–220/270 (8 slices) | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The mask overall looks reasonable, but there's an irregular leak superiorly in the coronal slices around 183-201. I'm considering a morphological opening with a small radius to clean up thin spikes and debris, then keeping the largest connected component, but I should check coronal slice 183 first to decide.

content.text: coronal 183/270 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The upper region near 3624/3571 is ambiguous—could be tumor extension along the muscle or just edema, and the edges leak near 4312/3908. I'll try adding negative points at those leaky edge coordinates to pull back the segmentation boundary there.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 1526.6 mL | components 23 (largest 99.9%; 22 others total 0.1 mL) | extent axial 214–495, coronal 74–235, sagittal 79–215 | change +35.1 mL / -66.9 mL | tool calls 8/40, prompts 2/15 | point erase (2 mark(s)) | image: axial 367, coronal 159, sagittal 151 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: There's still some small debris at the inferior end, and I'm checking a posterior intermediate signal region on axial 364 — it looks like edematous muscle (semimembranosus) rather than tumor, so I'll leave it out. For the inferior debris, I'll apply an opening with radius 2 and then keep only the largest connected component.

content.text: version v3 (parent v2) | volume 1517.0 mL | components 4 (largest 99.9%; 3 others total 0.8 mL) | extent axial 217–481, coronal 74–235, sagittal 79–215 | change +0.0 mL / -9.7 mL | tool calls 9/40, prompts 2/15 | edit open | image: axial 367, coronal 160, sagittal 151 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)
Keep the largest component.
axial 364/729 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v3 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: The protrusion near 2477 looks like a decent fit — that intermediate gray region between 2532 and 2519 could be part of the tumor, maybe a lobule. I'll keep this component paired with 2521.

content.text: version v4 (parent v3) | volume 1516.1 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 234–481, coronal 74–235, sagittal 79–215 | change +0.0 mL / -0.8 mL | tool calls 11/40, prompts 2/15 | edit keep_component | image: axial 367, coronal 160, sagittal 151 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: There's still a disconnected piece below the main lesion extending out of plane, with the inferior boundary reaching around slice 234. I should check axial slices near this inferior end, roughly 260-300, and cross-reference against the sagittal view to pin down where the mask actually terminates, since the display scaling makes it tricky to judge exact coordinates.

content.text: sheet axial 236–320/729 (8 slices) | v4 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: I'm trying to distinguish edema from true tumor at the inferior tail, since the feathery striated signal at 236-290 looks like muscle edema rather than mass, while 296-308 appears more homogeneous, suggesting the tumor's true inferior border sits around slice 300.

content.text: axial 292/729 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v4 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
The masked core at slice 292 looks slightly brighter and smooth, which could fit a tapering tumor pole or tail — myxoid tumors like myxofibrosarcoma are known for this "tail sign" along fascial planes, which radiologists often flag.

I'm uncertain how far the mask should extend; below ~270 it looks feathery and should be erased, while 272 and 284 still show modest bright blobs. I'll settle on erasing the 234-265 range as a compromise.

content.text: version v5 (parent v4) | volume 1503.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 266–481, coronal 74–235, sagittal 79–215 | change +0.0 mL / -12.6 mL | tool calls 14/40, prompts 2/15 | paint erase on 36 slice(s) | image: axial 368, coronal 160, sagittal 151 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm pinning the superior extent at 481, noting the sagittal spike at the top, then cross-checking against the axial slices from 430 to 481 to confirm.

content.text: sheet axial 410–485/729 (8 slices) | v5 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I'm reconsidering the orientation - the femur appears at lower right in these slices, with tissue posterior-medial to it showing bright lobules at 410-431 that could be tumor. Then at slice 464, the mask only partially covers a bright rounded lobule in the anterior region around 940-1010.

At 474/485 there's a bright oval structure anterior to the hip that could be the iliopsoas muscle with edema, or possibly tumor extension, and at 442 there's another bright region medially near the pubis/pectineus area that's worth examining more closely. I want to zoom into axial slice 464 to get a clearer look.

content.text: axial 462/729 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v5 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: The upper oval structure is too blurry to interpret clearly—it could be a lobulated tumor lobule or a vessel bundle. I should check a sagittal slice through the superior part of the mass, around sagittal index 151 where there's a spike, or better yet view a coronal slice through that superior pole to clarify.

content.text: sagittal 155/270 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v5 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: The mask looks like it matches, with that superior tip near 3763 likely being a lobule, which seems acceptable. Let me check other candidates.

content.text:
Final review of v5: volume 1503.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 266–481, coronal 74–235, sagittal 79–215 | tool calls 19/40, prompts 2/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 781 mL, touches mask on its left, right and posterior sides, level with the mask
C2 add 759 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C3 add 655 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C4 add 104 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
C5 add 1.0 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "4296" to save it.

content.thinking: Sample 113 has a small stray strip posterior but it's part of the same component, so that's a minor issue I can accept.

arguments.reason: Mask follows the bright lobulated mass in all planes; the edges at the inferior edema-like tail and superior pole are uncertain.

content.text: case M23 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v5 | final volume 1503.5 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 20/40, prompts 2/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I've saved the mask for the myxoid tumor (version v5) with medium confidence: about 1,504 mL as a single connected piece. The outline follows the bright lobulated mass in all three planes. The two ends are the uncertain part.

- **Location and size:** a large mass in the medial thigh, mostly in front of and beside the femur. It runs about 215 mm along the leg, from axial slice 266 up to slice 481, near the hip.
- **How it was built:** four positive points on the bright mass produced the first mask. That mask leaked upward toward the pelvis, so I erased the leak with two negative points. I then trimmed thin spurs and loose fragments with a small morphological opening and kept only the largest piece.
- **Lower end (uncertain):** below the mass the muscle shows streaky bright signal that looks like swelling (edema) rather than tumor, so I erased the mask below slice 266. Slices 266–295 are still included because the tissue there looks like a tapering, fairly uniform tip of the mass. That part could also be swollen muscle, or the tumor could reach further down.
- **Upper end (uncertain):** the mask ends in a narrow lobule near the hip at slice 481. At about slice 462 there is a rounded lobule next to the mask, mostly outside it, that I couldn't clearly tell apart from normal hip structures, so I left it out.
- **Included but uncertain:** at slices 410–431 the mask includes a band of tissue curving behind the femur, because it contains small bright nodules that look like tumor.
- **Rejected suggestions:** all five automatic suggestions for missed tissue were rings of surrounding fat, fascia and muscle around the mass, or scattered fragments above it, so I didn't add any of them.

I used 20 of 40 tool calls and 2 of 15 model prompts.
